title: Barn / OpenGrants: grant programs with milestone reviews and capped payouts
summary: A sponsor runs a grant program and awards a grant to a developer's project; the developer adds milestones, submits them for review, and the sponsor accepts and pays each one, never beyond the grant.
what: Barn (OpenGrants) puts the grant workflow on chain. Every wallet creates one profile with a username. A profile approved as a **sponsor** can create grant programs and award one grant per project, in SOL or an SPL token, with an approved amount. A **developer** profile creates projects, adds milestones with an amount against their grant, and submits each for review. The sponsor sends it back, rejects it or accepts it, and **settles** an accepted milestone, paying it from the sponsor's own wallet. The program keeps a running `paid_out` and refuses any payment that would exceed the grant. All records are PDAs numbered by a counter on their parent, and everything human-readable lives in a JSON file at each account's `uri`.
app_note: The fork's own Next.js 14 app as a static export with this devnet program ID. Per-account pages are `/project/view/?a=<address>` (and likewise for programs and profiles) because pages for accounts created later can't be pre-rendered. Sample metadata files for the URI fields are served at `/dapps/barn/meta/` (sponsor.json, dev.json, program.json, project.json, grant.json, milestone.json). Script: [tests/devnet/patches/barn.py](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/patches/barn.py). You need **two wallets**, one sponsor and one developer.

diagram:
wallet ─ create_user(seed, uri) ─▶ Authority PDA [wallet]  ──points to──▶ Profile PDA ["profile", seed]  (sponsor: false, count)
anyone ─ approve_sponsor() ─▶ profile.sponsor = true   (only while profile.count == 0)
sponsor ─ add_grant_program(uri) ─▶ GrantProgram PDA ["grant-program", profile, profile.count]
dev ───── add_project(uri) ──────▶ Project PDA ["project", profile, profile.count]   grant: None
sponsor ─ award_grant(uri, approved_amount) ─▶ Grant PDA ["grant", grant_program, program.count]  payment_mint, approved_amount, paid_out = 0
dev ───── add_grant_milestone(uri, amount) ─▶ GrantMilestone PDA ["grant-milestone", grant, grant.count]  InProgress
dev ───── review ─▶ InReview      sponsor ─ revise ─▶ InProgress | accept ─▶ Accepted | reject ─▶ (see the bug)
sponsor ─ settle_grant_milestone() ─▶ paid_out + amount ≤ approved_amount ? pay sponsor → dev, Paid : ApprovedAmountExceeded
accounts: Which profile this wallet controls (one per wallet, ever)
Sponsor flag, counter of programs or projects, metadata URI
Developer profile, the one grant it may receive
Project, payment mint, approved amount, paid out, milestone count
Amount, state (InProgress, InReview, Rejected, Accepted, Paid)

instructions.name: `create_user` and `approve_sponsor`: identities and roles
steps: Two PDAs: one at the wallet's own address bytes (`seeds=[signer]`), so a wallet can only ever have one; one at `["profile", username]`, so usernames are unique (a taken one fails with account already in use, in Proof).

`approve_sponsor` has an `admin: Signer` that nothing checks: any wallet can approve any profile, as long as that profile has no projects yet (`ProfileCannotBeSponsor`). Our script did it with an unrelated wallet; in the app, the sponsor approved itself.

instructions.name: Programs and projects: role-gated, counter-numbered
steps: `constraint=profile.sponsor` / `!profile.sponsor` gates who may call (`NotASponsor`, `NotADev`, in Proof).
The new account's address includes `profile.count` (little-endian u32), and `count` is incremented in the same instruction, so addresses are 0, 1, 2… per profile without collisions.

instructions.name: `award_grant`: one grant per project
steps: The grant program must be the signer's own (its seeds include `profile`).
`receive_grant` requires `project.grant` to be `None` (`GrantAlreadyAwarded`, in Proof).
The payment mint is stored; the app always uses the native mint (wrapped SOL), i.e. SOL.

instructions.name: Milestones: a small state machine
steps: Only the grant's developer adds milestones; the amount is **not** checked against the grant here (our #1 of 0.01 SOL was accepted although only 0.005 remained).
review → InReview; revise → InProgress; accept → Accepted; reject → Rejected. Once Rejected, Accepted or Paid (`confirmed()`), nothing can change it (`MilestoneAlreadyConfirmed`, in Proof).
`check_signer` ties a sponsor to the grant's program and a developer to the project.

instructions.name: `settle_grant_milestone`: pay, capped by the grant
steps: First `grant.settle_milestone(amount)`: `paid_out + amount` must stay ≤ `approved_amount` (`ApprovedAmountExceeded`). Then the milestone must be Accepted (`MilestoneNotAccepted`) and becomes Paid.

SOL grants: a System Program transfer from the signer to `to`; tokens: `transfer_checked` from the signer's token account. The money comes from the sponsor's wallet at that moment; nothing is escrowed.
Our script: grant 0.02 SOL, #0 0.015 paid (dev +0.015 SOL); #0 again → `ApprovedAmountExceeded` (the cap check runs before the Paid check); #1 0.01 → 0.025 > 0.02 → `ApprovedAmountExceeded`.

innovation.title: counter-numbered PDAs as an on-chain database
innovation.text: Barn has no list accounts. Each parent keeps a `count`, and each child lives at `[kind, parent, count]`, so profile → programs/projects → grants → milestones form a tree that any client can walk by deriving addresses 0…count−1, and every relationship is checked by re-deriving seeds in the account constraints. The money rule is one line: `paid_out + amount ≤ approved_amount`.

refs.note: grant numbered by its program's count

more: Roles and wiring matter as much as the cap. Line 55–57 of `lib.rs` sends `reject_grant_milestone` to `accept_milestone()`. We read the milestone our script "rejected" (#2, Gy5XhNzw…) on devnet: its state byte is 3, **Accepted**. A rejected milestone can therefore still be paid (Exercise 1). The settle accounts also never tie `grant` to the signer's own program or `to` to the developer (Exercise 3).

frontend.title: One hook per instruction
steps: The app calls the fork's own TypeScript client (`protocol/ts`), which builds each instruction with `accountsPartial` and lets Anchor derive the PDAs.

frontend.title: Approve Sponsor: any wallet as admin
steps: `admin: wallet.publicKey`: whoever is connected.

frontend.title: Award Grant: always SOL
steps: `paymentMint = NATIVE_MINT // todo: any token`; the amount is SOL × 10⁹.

frontend.title: Settle Payment
steps: The app sets `to` to the project owner's wallet, so it pays the right person; the program doesn't require that.

exercises.title: Fix Reject
steps: Look at `lib.rs` lines 55–57 and `update_grant_milestone.rs` line 67.
Change `reject_grant_milestone` to call `ctx.accounts.reject_milestone()`, rebuild, and reject a milestone in a local test.
exercises.expect: Its state becomes Rejected (2). Before the fix, our devnet milestone Gy5XhNzw… reads 3 (Accepted) after "reject", and a sponsor could settle it.
exercises.hint: Look at `lib.rs` around the `reject_grant_milestone` entry point, and at the handler it actually calls.
exercises.approach: Change it to call `ctx.accounts.reject_milestone()` (the handler that sets state 2), rebuild, and reject a milestone on a local validator. Its state should become Rejected (2). Before the fix, our devnet milestone Gy5XhNzw… reads 3 (Accepted) after 'reject', and a sponsor could settle it.

exercises.title: Gate Approve Sponsor
steps: Add a constant `ADMIN` and `address = ADMIN` on `admin` in `approve_sponsor.rs`.
exercises.expect: Our script's approval by an unrelated wallet (4jemNXkW…) would fail with a constraint error; only the admin can create sponsors.
exercises.hint: `approve_sponsor` has an `admin: Signer` that nothing constrains — any wallet can approve any eligible profile.
exercises.approach: Add a constant `ADMIN` and `address = ADMIN` on that signer (or a PDA config). The script's approval by an unrelated wallet should then fail; only the admin should be able to create sponsors.

exercises.title: Tie settle to the right grant and payee
steps: In `SettleGrantMilestone`, load the grant program and project and add `grant.program == grant_program.key()`, `grant_program.profile == profile.key()`, `project.key() == grant.project`, and require `to` to be the project owner's wallet.
Locally: a second sponsor settles the first sponsor's accepted milestone with `to` = itself.
exercises.expect: Rejected after the fix. Before it, the call succeeds: the second sponsor pays itself, the milestone is marked Paid and the developer can never be paid for it.
exercises.hint: `settle` pays `to`, which is an account the client passes. The program should require it to be the project's owner, and the grant to belong to that program.
exercises.approach: Load the grant program and the project, and add `grant.program == grant_program.key()`, `grant_program.profile == profile.key()`, and `to.key() == project.owner` (or whatever the field is called). A settle that names a different payee should fail; the recorded 0.005 SOL settle to the developer should still pass.

exercises.title: Check milestone amounts when they're added
steps: In `add_milestone`, sum existing milestone amounts (or keep a `committed` total on the grant) and refuse when it would exceed `approved_amount`.
exercises.expect: Our milestone #1 (0.01 SOL with 0.005 left) is refused at creation instead of failing only at settle.
exercises.hint: A milestone can be added for more than the remaining grant. The cap is only checked at settle.
exercises.approach: At `add_grant_milestone`, `require!(granted.paid_out + existing_milestones + new_amount <= approved_amount)`. Adding a milestone that would overflow the grant should then fail early, before anyone reviews it.

exercises.title: Clearer double-settle error
steps: In `settle_milestone`, call `self.grant_milestone.settle()` before `self.grant.settle_milestone(..)`, and in `settle()` return `MilestoneAlreadyPaid` when the state is Paid.
exercises.expect: Settling #0 twice now fails with `MilestoneAlreadyPaid` instead of `ApprovedAmountExceeded`.
exercises.hint: A second settle of a paid milestone may fail for a generic reason (already closed, wrong state) rather than a named error.
exercises.approach: Add `require!(milestone.state == Accepted)` (not Paid) and a `MilestoneAlreadyPaid` error. A second settle should return that error; the first remains the recorded 3PUJ7ZJm….

not_covered: The whole sponsor → developer → milestone → payment flow was clicked through in the app with two wallets. Revise, reject, the cap and every rejection case were run by script. Note: "reject" actually accepts in this program (Exercise 1; checked on devnet: milestone Gy5XhNzw… is Accepted after reject). Not exercised: SPL-token grants (the app only awards SOL), edit_grant_milestone.
objectives: Walk a tree of counter-numbered PDAs: profile → program/project → grant → milestone, each derived from its parent and a count.
See a payout cap enforced in one line: `paid_out + amount ≤ approved_amount`.
Find, and fix, `reject_grant_milestone` calling `accept_milestone()` — proven on devnet, where the 'rejected' milestone is Accepted.
prereqs: Two wallets (sponsor and developer) and about 0.05 SOL in the sponsor's.
Stage 2 up through [Votara](/lessons/votara/) (counters, roles). This is the most structured state machine so far.
